title: A Depth‐Averaged Discontinuous Galerkin Morphodynamic Model With Orthogonal Bubble Function‐Based Boundary Treatment
content:
Abstract

A discontinuous Galerkin (DG) model is developed for river morphodynamic simulations based on a depth-averaged coupled shallow-water–Exner formulation, in which the hydrodynamics are described by the shallow water equations, while the bedload transport rate is evaluated using the Wong–Parker bedload relation and the bed evolution is updated through the Exner equation. A Hasegawa-type bedload-direction correction is further introduced to represent the effects of curvature-induced secondary flow and transverse bed slope on the direction of bedload transport. The model features an improved boundary treatment using orthogonal bubble function elements. The proposed framework utilizes linear triangular elements in the interior domain and specialized orthogonal bubble function elements along solid boundaries, enabling accurate and stable enforcement of the no-normal-flow condition. In addition, a nodal-normal-based treatment is introduced to ensure a smooth and continuous representation of solid boundaries. These boundary treatments provide robust numerical solutions for sediment transport processes near riverbanks. Benchmark tests, laboratory validation cases, and a field-scale application demonstrate mesh- and time-step-convergent solutions, reasonable agreement with measured bed deformation, and stable computation over a realistic river geometry. The results also show that including the Hasegawa-type correction can improve the predicted erosion–deposition patterns in curved channels. The results indicate that the proposed DG framework provides a promising and robust basis for coupled hydrodynamic–morphodynamic simulations in riverine settings and can be further extended to more complex hydro-morphodynamic processes.
